blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Industrial Equipment & Machinery. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Equipment makers pivot to outcome businesses: connected machines, service contracts and uptime guarantees replace box sales. The pivot is an engineering program — fleet connectivity, service intelligence and outcome pricing — built once, monetized for decades.

items: Connected machinery inherits product-security duties (EU CRA); firmware estates unmanaged.
Machines in the field lack telemetry; service is reactive and parts planning blind.

blocks.x: The pattern composes AI Security & Model Protection, Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust, Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Fleet connectivity/OTA, Service dispatch and parts, Outcome/uptime contracts) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — EU Machinery Regulation/CRA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Assume breach, plan recovery: resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.
Evidence once, audit anywhere: compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy.
SBOM, signed firmware, vulnerability SLAs (CRA duties evidenced)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: restoration-tested backups and manual-fallback procedures for production lines (recovery time proven in drills). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
